See also: Soleil

English

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

Borrowed from French soleil.

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • Audio (US):(file)

Noun

[edit]

soleil

  1. (Polari) sun
    • 1967, Kenneth Horne, Bona Bijou Tourettes (Round the Horne), season 3, episode 12:
      Divine. ... Disporting yourself on the sable plage getting your lallies all bronzed - your riah getting bleached by the soleil.

Related terms

[edit]
  • brise soleil

French

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

Inherited from Middle French soleil, from Old French soleil, from Vulgar Latin *sōliculus, diminutive of Latin sōl (“sun”), from Proto-Indo-European *sóh₂wl̥.

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): /sɔ.lɛj/, /so.lɛj/
  • Audio (France):(file)
  • Audio (Switzerland (Valais)):(file)
  • Audio (France (Paris)):(file)
  • Audio (France (Toulouse)):(file)
  • Audio (France (Vosges)):(file)
  • Audio (France):(file)
  • Audio (France (Grenoble)):(file)
  • Audio (France (Vosges)):(file)
  • Audio (France (Vosges)):(file)
  • Audio (France (Hérault)):(file)
  • Audio (France (Lyon)):(file)
  • Audio (France (Massy)):(file)
  • Audio (France (Somain)):(file)
  • Rhymes: -ɛj

Noun

[edit]

soleil m (plural soleils)

  1. sun (star)
    Il fait soleil.
    It is sunny.
    Regarder le soleil fait mal aux yeux.
    Looking at the sun hurts the eyes.
  2. sunflower
    Synonym: tournesol

Derived terms

[edit]
  • bain de soleil
  • carte soleil
  • coucher de soleil
  • coup de soleil
  • fondre comme neige au soleil
  • lever du soleil
  • lunettes de soleil
  • pays du Soleil Levant
  • prendre le soleil
  • rien de nouveau sous le soleil
  • soleil de minuit
  • soleil de plomb
  • soleil mexicain
  • un-deux-trois-soleil

Related terms

[edit]
  • solaire
  • solarium

Further reading

[edit]
  • “soleil”, in Trésor de la langue française informatisé [Digitized Treasury of the French Language], 2012

Old French

[edit]

Alternative forms

[edit]
  • souleil, soloil

Etymology

[edit]

From Vulgar Latin *sōliculus, diminutive of Latin sōl (“sun”), from Proto-Indo-European *sóh₂wl̥. Compare Old Occitan solelh.

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): /suˈleʎ/

Noun

[edit]

soleil oblique singular, m (oblique plural soleuz or soleilz, nominative singular soleuz or soleilz, nominative plural soleil)

  1. sun (star)

Descendants

[edit]
  • Gallo: soulai
  • Franc-Comtois: soroiye
  • Middle French: soleil
    • French: soleil
  • Norman: solé
  • Walloon: solea
